Sampling V6 concise report

Choosing a Sampling Method Under Session Caps

Population context: 2,800 sessions across 105 agents, spanning dense_2500, historical_300 corpora with 30 paired seeds. ARM2 uses Azure Search for donor retrieval, and use-case coverage remains provisional because the Maven labels are classification-derived and some assignments are Ambiguous.

Population
2,800 sessions
Agents
105 agents
Corpora
dense_2500 / historical_300

How to read: MAE is the absolute error between the estimator and the full-population benchmark. Concept coverage is the proportion of distinct source concepts in the full population represented by at least one sampled session; higher is better for representation, but it is not the same as MAE or Maven business-use-case coverage.

Decision at a glance

Low-cap / high-cap pattern

At the low-cap end (64 sessions), ARM1 Global Random has the lowest MAE (0.0417) while ARM2 Embedding IDW, ARM3 Agent Round Robin Floor, ARM4 Agent Round Robin, ARM5 Hajek Weighted are tied for broadest concept coverage (13.33%). At the high-cap end (1024 sessions), ARM5 Hajek Weighted remains the best combined MAE/coverage balance at 1024 sessions, so the decision stays conditional: choose the lowest MAE when the budget is tight, but treat concept coverage as the representativeness guardrail when broader source coverage matters more than a small MAE gain.

What is measured

Use the fixed-population evidence correctly
MAE
Lower is better
Absolute difference from the census benchmark at a cap.
Concept coverage
Higher is broader
Share of distinct source concepts in the full population that are represented by at least one sampled session.
Limit
Not general inference
This is descriptive evidence for this synthetic population and cap grid, not a claim about all sessions everywhere.

Five techniques

Selection and estimator are not the same

ARM1

StepsDraw sessions uniformly across the fixed population; keep the selected set simple and budgeted.
EstimatorUnweighted sample mean for the pass-rate estimate.
StrengthSimple, robust low-cap baseline with minimal tuning.
RiskCan miss concept-rich regions when a few hot agents dominate the population.
Choose whenUse as the clean baseline when the goal is speed and low complexity under a strict cap.

ARM2

StepsUse embedding similarity and the Azure Search donor pool, then apply same-agent IDW for unjudged units.
EstimatorSame-agent IDW plus donor-weighted adjustment rather than a raw mean.
StrengthLocal fidelity and calibration when similar sessions are available.
RiskEmbedding or search quality can dominate the result and amplify duplication risk.
Choose whenChoose this when donor quality matters and the objective emphasizes explicit imputation quality.

ARM3

StepsEnforce a floor to protect agent coverage, then allocate the remaining budget across Maven strata.
EstimatorUnweighted mean across the selected sessions.
StrengthBroad representation and a minimum floor before the cap is consumed.
RiskSome of the cap is spent on coverage protection instead of pure MAE minimization.
Choose whenChoose it when broad representation is a non-negotiable requirement.

ARM4

StepsRound-robin across agents and then balance by Maven strata without a hard floor.
EstimatorUnweighted mean.
StrengthGood agent diversity and concept spread under the cap.
RiskUse-case strata can still miss rare concept pockets if the strata are noisy.
Choose whenChoose it when diversity and representation matter more than an exact floor guarantee.

ARM5

StepsUse the same membership as ARM4, but switch the estimator to a Hajek ratio estimator.
EstimatorWeighted ratio estimate that respects selection propensities.
StrengthPreserves ARM4 coverage while improving estimator design alignment.
RiskLow-cap weighting can be unstable and slightly raise MAE.
Choose whenChoose it when you want ARM4-style coverage with a more design-aware estimator.

Results story

Visual-first view

Takeaway: the best method changes by cap and objective. Low-cap comparisons are most sensitive to the estimator choice, while high-cap patterns let broader representativeness and lower MAE coexist without claiming a universal winner.

Interactive explorer

Metric tabs, method toggles, aggregate or trial mode

Conclusion

Conditioned on the fixed bundle

Recommendation: If the objective is a tight-cap, low-error baseline, prefer the method with the lowest MAE at the active cap. If the objective is representativeness across source concepts and agents, favor the method with the highest concept coverage at that cap, while acknowledging that concept coverage is not accuracy and not a proxy for Maven business-use-case coverage. On this bundle, the pattern is clear: low-cap decisions are driven mainly by MAE, while high-cap decisions can lower MAE and increase concept coverage without implying a single universal winner.
